messages:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking we should version the pool-controller API rather than continuously extending query params. v1 served us, but drift is making operator shims messy. TL;DR: split admit/telemetry readonly surface (stable) from execution/evict/scale surface (v2) and give a migration path.
Maya: +1 to explicit versioning. can you sketch migration steps? worried about tenants pinning old behavior. :thinking_face:
Sam: migration sketch: 1) introduce v2 endpoints that are opt-in, 2) enable dual-write to both controllers for X weeks, 3) rollout canary for 10% of tenants + feature flag, 4) flip default after regression-free window.
Liam: sounds good. question: do we keep the same resource /pools/{id}/admit or change path to /v2/pools/{id}/admit? We need minimal router churn for Dedicated.
Nina: prefer path-based versions (/v2/...) so proxies can route without header magic. header-based versioning is fine for internal RPCs though.
Sam: agree path-based for public HTTP surface. internal RPCs (controller <-> operator) could use explicit proto version in metadata. avoids tearing at LB.
Maya: tradeoffs: path-versioning requires API gateway rules per version, more infra work. header-based lets us do gradual rollout by header injection at edge. either way, we need compatibility adapters in the operator for a while.
Liam: another concern — admission is latency-sensitive. If we route admit to v2 but fallback to v1 under load, we need a clear contract about determinism and idempotency. eviction/scale ops are eventually consistent so easier.
Sam: good point. propose we keep admit READ path strictly backward compatible for 6 months. v2 can add additional signals (packing hints, tenant-history) but must not break decision IDs.
Nina: also add explicit schema version in the admit response: {"schema_v": "1"} so clients can detect behavior drift and fallback heuristics.
Maya: +1. Also add smoke-e2e that compares decisions across v1/v2 on sampled traffic to detect regressions automatically. ops-bot can alert if divergence > 1% over 10k requests.
ops-bot: alert rule created: pool-controller-schema-divergence > 1% over 10k samples => pager to #eng-runtime-oncall.
Liam: implementation note: operator side needs to support dual-run mode: accept v1 requests, pass through to legacy allocator, and optionally call v2 planner in parallel to validate results. That adds CPU cost but only during migration window.
Sam: agreed. add a config toggle: planner-validation.disabled=false by default in canary. We can ramp down.
Maya: can we avoid dual-run cost by running v2 planner in a dedicated validation job that replays admit decisions asynchronously? That won't catch racey edge cases though.
Nina: the async replay is cheaper but slower to catch regressions. I'd prefer dual-run for the 10% canary then replay for the wider 50% window.
Liam: ops question: metrics & logs — we should tag all metrics with api_version and canary_bucket. Then optimize dashboards to compare p99 admit latency and acceptance rates between versions.
Sam: yes. add metric names: pool.admit.latency_ms{api_version=v1|v2, tenant_bucket=canary|control}. Also emit decision.hash to correlate.
Maya: rollout checklist proposal (short): 1) API spec + openapi diff, 2) gateway routing rules, 3) dual-run operator + feature flag, 4) smoke-e2e + divergence alerts, 5) canary 10% (2 weeks), 6) replay validation 50% (2 weeks), 7) flip default + monitor 4 weeks, 8) deprecate v1 after 6 months.
Nina: add migration doc for customers: how to opt-in/out and how to verify behavior. Also include a note on rate limits changes if v2 adds batching hints.
Sam: thanks. can someone volunteer to draft the openapi diff and the migration doc? I can own the operator dual-run changes.
Maya: I can draft the openapi diff + sample client snippet.
Liam: I can write the metrics/dashboards + canary automation.
Nina: I'll own the migration doc and customer comms.
Sam: great. next action: Maya to drop a PR with openapi diff by EOD Thursday. Liam/Nina/Maya — meet sync Friday 10am to align on canary gating metrics.
Maya: noted.
deploy-bot: Scheduled meeting created: "Pool-controller API versioning sync" Fri 10:00 — invites sent to Sam, Maya, Liam, Nina.
Sam: thanks all. leaving a short RFC link in #docs when PR lands. :thumbsup:
